gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Noto Sans Hebrew fills its line with a dominant midsection and leaves wide gaps where curves meet stems. Nippo, cut from wire with ruler-straight strokes, feels like the sharper sibling.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-hk: Technical and contemporary, Nippo draws small letters nearly capital-sized, curves and straights sharing a single width. Noto Sans HK, with large lowercase and brush ends lifted before curves close, keeps text moving without snagging.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-jp: Nippo looks cut from wire, bars and stems matching exactly. Where it does best is stamping a technical look; Noto Sans JP, with a very high x-height and sweeping curves, is better at carrying text.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Contemporary and technical, Nippo has no hairlines and no swells, only wire-cut strokes. Noto Sans Kaithi, a sans-serif whose lowercase fills the line like capitals, sits next to it as the broader, plainer counterpart.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Blunt, marker-drawn, wire-cut: Nippo stands its small letters nearly capital-sized. Noto Sans Khojki, a sans with wide exits and a large eye on every e, brings the pair its openness.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-kr: Generous gaps in the curves and stubby ascenders make Noto Sans KR a sans that reads openly. And Nippo, with every stroke cut uniformly, gives it a crisp, technical partner up top.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-lao: Nippo draws small letters nearly capital-sized, with an unbroken line width on every letter. But Noto Sans Lao, a sans-serif with its x-height pushed high and open mouths, is where the pair finds its clarity.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Technical and contemporary, Nippo keeps a ballpoint's plain, pressure-free line, its small, proud letters standing almost capital-sized. Nippo makes statements; Noto Sans Lepcha, wide-curved with cast-iron lowercase, holds conversations.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Nippo keeps its small letters nearly capital-sized, with no vertical emphasis and no horizontal thinning. Then Noto Sans Limbu, a sans with gaping curves and long-bodied lowercase, relaxes the page around it.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-mahajani: Nippo has strokes like a bent paperclip, and small letters nearly capital-sized. Noto Sans Mahajani, a sans-serif with a funnel-wide e and sturdy lowercase, should read smoothly paragraph after paragraph.
